title: Tracking and characterization of partial and full epithelial-mesenchymal transition cells in a mouse model of metastatic breast cancer
protocol: Sterilize surfaces, forceps, scalpels, and surgical scissors with 70% ethanol.
Euthanize the mouse using CO2.
Dissect mammary tumors: Place mouse on its back, stretch-out and pin-down on all four limbs.
Spray the abdomen with 70% ethanol and wipe-off excess liquid.
Use forceps and a surgical scissor to make an incision extending from the bottom of the abdomen to the thorax.
Extend the incision along the limbs to create an x-shape.
Separate the skin from the peritoneum to expose the tumors.
Using two forceps, gently pull the skin to the sides and use a scalpel to separate it from the abdomen if necessary.
Pin down the stretched-out skin.
Using a scalpel, dissect all individual mammary tumors and the surrounding mammary fat pad.
Prepare paraffin and/or OCT frozen tissue blocks with 1–2 pieces (3–5 mm in diameter) of tumors from individual mammary tumors as described by Lüönd and Sugiyama et al.
Store prepared tumor blocks at room temperature or -80°C for later use.
Collect tumors from multiple locations for sliced tissue culture and for single-cell isolation.
Using a 10 mL syringe, pour warm (≈ 37°C) 3% low-melting agarose solution into a Peel-A-Way histology mold to make a thin layer of agarose.
Place the mold on ice.
Wait for the agarose to solidify in approximately 5 minutes.
Place one piece of tumor on top of solidified agarose.
Cover the tumor with 5–6 mL of agarose solution until tissue is entirely covered.
Optimize the position of the blade using the VibroCheck on the Leica VT 1200S vibratome.
Secure the optimized blade into the blade holder.
Spray the specimen disc and buffer tray of the Leica VT 1200S vibratome with 70% ethanol.
Glue the face of the upper side of the agarose block directly to the specimen disc.
Wait for glue to dry completely (3–5 min).
Place the buffer tray into the ice holder of the Leica VT 1200S vibratome.
Fill the buffer tray with ice-cold sterile PBS and add ice into the ice holder.
Once sample embedded in agarose has adhered to the specimen disc, place the disc into the buffer tray.
Set the ice tray onto the vibratome stand and lock the tray in place by moving the lever to the right.
Raise the stage until the blade touches the surface of the agarose gel using the control pad.
Set cutting window on the vibratome.
Set section thickness to auto feed (250–350 μm) on the vibratome.
Set amplitude to 1–2 mm on the vibratome.
Set speed to 0.1–1.0 mm/s on the vibratome.
Run the vibratome at 1.0 mm/s until the blade reaches the tissue.
Adjust settings depending on the consistency and integrity of the tissue.
Cut tumors at amplitude 2 mm, speed 0.1 mm/s in most cases.
Gently scoop uniform slices out of the bath using spatulas or forceps once obtained.
Clean spatulas and forceps with 70% ethanol prior to use.
Transfer tumor slices into a 6-well plate containing 2–3 mL ice-cold DMEM/F12 medium on ice.
Place the plate on ice.
Scoop up one slice from each piece of tumor using a sterile spatula.
Place each slice into one well of a 24-well plate.
Add 300 μL pre-warmed DMEM/F12 medium containing Alexa Fluor-conjugated antibody (e.g., Alexa Fluor 647 anti-mouse CD31, 1:50) to the slices.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Place one Millicell Cell Culture insert into each well of a 24-well imaging plate using sterile forceps.
Pipette 300 μL of DMEM/F12 medium for breast tumor slice tissue into the well and 50 μL into the insert.
Wash the tissue slices by transferring them twice through separate wells containing 500 μL of pre-warmed DMEM/F12 medium using forceps.
Gently transfer one slice onto one cell culture insert using forceps.
Use a spatula to gently spread the slice to ensure it lays completely flat on the cell insert membrane.
Remove excess media from the insert to the outer well if necessary to avoid floating and folding of the slice in the insert.
Add sterile water or PBS to one row of wells on each of the four surrounding sides of the plate for imaging.
Fill the spaces between wells with sterile water or PBS if more than 8 wells are needed for culture.
Switch on all components of the spinning disc confocal microscope.
Turn on the computer.
Set up the incubation chamber at 37°C with 5% CO2, 90 ± 5% humidity.
Switch on the individual lasers by turning on the keys.
Start VisiView Premier Image acquisition Software.
Place the imaging plate containing the tissue culture inserts on the microscope stage.
Open “Acquisition” panel in VisiView Premier.
Set up the exposure time for every channel and pixel binning as “2”.
Go to “Wavelength” tab and tick “Wavelength series” box.
Select the number of channels and lasers that should be active during acquisition.
Go to “Time-lapse” tab and tick “time-lapse series” box.
Set up the time interval and the duration of the acquisition for tissue slices.
Turn on the Perfect Focus System (PFS) controller.
Tick “Autofocus always on” box in PFS settings.
Select “Autofocus on during waiting” option.
Go to “Z-series” tab and tick the “Z-plane series” box.
Manually define a plane of interest to set “Home position”.
Set “Top Offset” and “Bottom Offset” for region of interest.
Go to “Stage” tab and set multiple XYZ points.
Pause image acquisition at every 24 hours during long-term imaging.
Replace medium in the wells with fresh pre-warmed medium using a 200 μl pipette with long tips.
Open the script on ImageJ software.
Press “Run” in the ImageJ interface.
Browse and select the stk file for drift correction.
Set up Z spacing, number of timepoints, number of slices, first position, number of positions, name of different channels, and reference channel for registration.
Use mCherry as a reference channel for drift correction.
Press “OK” to start the correction process.
Visually inspect the XYZ position in Arivis Vision4D software.
Manually adjust the XYZ position using “drift correction” from “Data” submenu if necessary.
Crop the region of interest using “transformation gallery” from “Data” submenu.
Activate the “Track Cells and Particles” pipeline from Analysis panel.
Select GFP channel for tracking in “Input ROI” panel.
Set up diameter, probability threshold, and split sensitivity in “Blob finder” panel.
Check values by executing the pipeline using step-by-step tool.
Define minimum volume of the blob filter.
In “Tracking” panel, select “Brownian motion (Centroid)” in “Motion type”.
Set max distance 15 μm per hour.
Tick “Fusions” and “Divisions” boxes to follow a cell even if fused or divides simultaneously.
Check all settings using step-by-step tool.
Run the pipeline.
Open “Object” panel.
Select features for tracking consideration.
Export results as excel file.
Plot trajectories of GFP+ cells in tumors on excel.
Make scatter plot with smooth line chart using X and Y displacement values to start (μm).
Select tumor pieces from multiple individual tumors with different morphology to account for tumor heterogeneity for sliced tissue culture and frozen tissue/paraffin embedding.
Pool remaining tumor tissue and surrounding mammary fat pad for digestion and single cell isolation for RNA sequencing.
Collect mammary tumors from MMTV-PyMT, MMTV-PyMT/RC::FrePe/Tnc-CreERT2 or MMTV-PyMT/RC::FrePe/Cdh2-CreERT2 mice for negative controls and single stain control samples required for compensation.
Prepare single-cell suspensions from collected mammary tumors.
Freeze negative control cells in FBS containing 10% DMSO as cryomedium and store in liquid nitrogen.
Prepare 10 mL collagenase/trypsin solution per mouse and store it on ice.
Pool all remaining mamMARY tumors from an individual mouse for single cell isolation.
Do not remove adipose tissue surrounding tumors.
Place the mammary tumor tissue on the lid of a sterile petri dish.
Cut the tissue into small pieces (<1 mm) using a scalpel with a sterile blade.
Transfer the chopped-up tissue into a 50 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL of collagenase/trypsin solution.
Incubate at 37°C while shaking at 200 rpm for 1 h.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature (RT).
Discard the supernatant by carefully decanting the content of the tube.
Add 10 mL of DNase solution and tilt the tube up and down few times for 5 min at RT.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at RT.
Discard the supernatant by decanting the content of the tube.
Suspend the pellet in 20–40 mL of ice-cold FACS buffer and filter into a 50 mL Falcon tube using a 70 μm sterile cell strainer.
Smash the pieces of tumor on the strainer with a plunger of a 5 mL syringe.
Wash the strainer with FACS buffer several times.
Determine the total number of cells manually using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at RT.
Discard the supernatant and prepare single-cell suspension at 1 × 106–1 × 107 cells/mL in ice-cold FACS buffer.
Add blocking antibody (CD16/32, 1:100) to remove immune cells, endothelial cells and red blood cells.
Incubate for 5 min on ice.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at RT.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold FACS buffer maintaining a cell concentration of 1 × 10^6 to 1 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Add biotin-conjugated CD31, CD45, and Ter-119 antibodies (1:100 dilution) to the cell suspension.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Add 5 mL of ice-cold FACS buffer to the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold FACS buffer to reach a concentration of 1 × 10^7 cells/mL.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Wash 100 μL of Dynabeads biotin binder in 1 mL of FACS buffer.
Place washed Dynabeads in an EasySep Magnet and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the beads in 100 μL of FACS buffer.
Add 100 μL pre-washed Dynabeads per up to 10^7 total cells, scaling up if necessary.
Mix well and incubate on ice for 30 min.
Place the tube into an EasySep Magnet for 3 min.
Collect the supernatant by pouring it into a 15 mL falcon tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove dead cells using EasySep™ Dead Cell Removal (Annexin V) Kit: Resuspend the pellet in ice-cold Dead Cell Removal buffer at 1 × 10^8 cells/mL.
Transfer the suspension into a 5 mL polystyrene tube.
Add 50 μL of Dead Cell Removal (Annexin V) Cocktail and 50 μL of Biotin Selection Cocktail to 1 mL of cell suspension, scaling up if necessary.
Incubate for 3 min at room temperature.
Vortex RapidSpheres™ for 30 s.
Add 100 μL of RapidSpheres per 1 mL of sample.
Immediately add Dead Cell Removal buffer to top up the sample to 2.5 mL.
Place the tube into the EasySep Magnet for 3 min.
Pour the live-cell enriched supernatant into a 15 mL Falcon tube.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Stain with Fluorophore-conjugated antibodies.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in FACS buffer to adjust the cell suspension to 1 × 10^6 cells/100 μL.
Add 1 μL each of APC anti-mouse CD326 (EpCAM) and Brilliant Violet 650™ (BV650) Streptavidin per 100 μL suspension.
Incubate for 20 min on ice.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5–15 mL FACS buffer.
Aliquot 50 μL of sample cell suspension for each control sample.
Add 0.5 μL of Brilliant Violet 650™ Streptavidin or APC anti-mouse CD326 (Ep-CAM) in tube iii and tube iv, respectively.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to tubes i-iv.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL FACS buffer and store on ice in the dark until sorting.
Prepare compensation control samples.
Aliquot 50 μL suspension of negative control cells into four microcentrifuge tubes (i-iv).
Add 0.5 μL of APC anti-mouse CD326 (Ep-CAM) or Brilliant Violet 650™ Streptavidin in tubes iii and iv, respectively.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL FACS buffer and store on ice in the dark until sorting.
Incubate on ice for 20 min.
Add 1 mL of FACS buffer to tubes i-iv.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at RT.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL FACS buffer.
Store on ice in the dark until sorting.
Trypsinize mCherry+ and GFP+ cell lines to prepare single-cell suspensions.
Wash cells once with PBS.
Add trypsin and incubate at 37°C until cells detach.
After trypsinization, add 10 mL of complete DMEM high glucose medium.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at RT.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL–1 mL of FACS buffer depending on the size of the pellet.
Store tube v and vi on ice in the dark until sorting.
Filtrate the experimental sample and all control samples through a 40 μm mesh into 5 mL polystyrene tubes.
Add Draq7 to the experimental sample and Draq7 containing controls.
Start the FACSAria IIIc sorter.
Choose a nozzle size of 100 μm.
Set up the side stream and optimize the position of the side streams for 4-way sort using the voltage sliders.
Set up the laser and the following filters: Draq7 (Laser: Red 633 nm, Mirror: 735LP, Filter: 780/60).
Apply negative control to set baselines for all channels.
Analyze compensation controls to select appropriate laser power and outputs for each fluorophore used.
Calculate and apply compensation.
Set up the sorting gates using experimental control samples.
Load non-stained experimental control step 58a (i) onto the FACSAria IIIc and verify that the sample cells contain mCherry and GFP-expressing cells.
Set up the gating by selecting the cellular compartment in the Forward Scatter Area (FSC-A) versus Side Scatter Area (SSC-A) dot plot.
Exclude doublets and aggregates using FSC-A and FSC-height (FSC-H).
Set up a gate for the negative fraction for Draq7.
Set up a gate for the negative cells for BV650 Streptavidin (biotinylated-CD31, CD45, and Ter119).
Analyze Draq7 control (experimental control step 58a (ii)) to ensure the selection of live cells.
Analyze APC-FMO control (experimental control step 58a (iii)) to ensure that the gates for live Lin- cells are set correctly.
Set up gates for mCherry+, GFP+, and double positive (mCherry+ GFP+) cells.
Set up gating for EpCAM- cells in each mCherry+, GFP+, and double positive populations.
Analyze BV650-FMO control to ensure the gates for EpCAM- cells are correct.
Set up gates for 3 populations of mCherry+ cells: mCherry+EpCAM-, mCherry+EpCAMhigh, and mCherryhighEpCAMhigh.
Set up gates for 4 populations of GFP+ cells: GFP+EpCAM-, GFP+EpCAMlow, GFP+EpCAMmed, and GFPhighEpCAMmed.
Set up gate for 1 population of double-positive cells: mCherry+ GFP+EpCAM+.
Open the sort collection chamber door and install 4 tubes containing 1 mL of FACS buffer on a 4-way chamber.
Insert the experimental sample in the sample injection chamber of the sorter.
Start acquisition and verify that the gate settings are correct.
Set up the desired number of events to collect.
Proceed with sorting 5K cells each for the 3 mCherry+ populations and the 1 mCherry+GFP+ double-positive population.
Collect GFP+ cells from mammary tumors for each of the 4 populations.
Centrifuge collected cells at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove supernatant, leaving approximately 200 μL of liquid.
Resuspend cells in collection tubes and keep on ice in the dark.
Set up volumes of samples as recommended by FACS facility or operator.
Optimize position of side streams for 96-well plates.
Place a MicroAmp Fast 96-Well Reaction Plate with a transparent lid on the stage in the sorting chamber.
Select Sort > Home Device to access the Device Setup dialog.
Select the desired collection device, such as "96 well-Falcon".
Click “Go to Home”.
Inspect the plate lid to see where a drop was deposited.
Wipe the lid dry and place it back onto the stage.
Adjust the Home location if the drop did not hit the center of the well.
Repeat inspection until the drop is centered appropriately.
Set up new Home position and check the location of drop deposition as above.
Clean a tissue culture hood with RNaseZap and DNA decontamination reagent before preparing a MicroAmp® Fast 96-Well Reaction Plate for RNA sequencing library preparation.
Clean pipettes with RNaseZap.
Pipette 2.3 μL of 0.2% TX-100 in PBS containing 2 U/μL RNase inhibitor into each well of a 96-well plate and store it on ice.
Cover the plate with RNAse free plate seal.
Clean the stage in the sorting chamber of FACSAria IIIc with RNaseZap.
Install the plate with well A1 toward the front of the stage.
Insert the sample tube in the sample injection chamber of the sorter.
Sort 3 tubes for mCherry+ populations.
Sort 4 tubes for GFP+ populations.
Sort 1 tube for double-positive populations.
Select target wells for 5-cell sorting.
Start acquisition and sort 5 cells per well on a MicroAmp® Fast 96-Well Reaction Plate.
Seal the plate with an adhesive plate seal after sorting.
Spin down the sealed plate.
Place the plate in a box containing dry ice.
Store the plate at −80°C as soon as possible until preparing libraries for RNA sequencing.
Spray the 96-well plate and cooling rack with RNaseZap to remove RNases.
Remove the adhesive seal from the 96-well plate.
Place the plate on the cooling rack on ice.
Prepare the annealing mixture by combining 90 μL H2O, 10 μL oligo-dT primer (10 μM), and 100 μL dNTP mix (10 mM each).
Add 2 μL of the annealing mix to each well containing a 5-cell pool in lysis buffer.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal after adding the mixture.
Vortex briefly to mix.
Spin down the sealed plate.
Incubate the plate at 72°C for 3 min.
Centrifuge the plate at 700 × g for 1 min.
Transfer the plate back on ice immediately afterward.
Prepare reverse transcription (RT) reaction mix.
Add 5.7 μL of RT mix to the samples.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal, vortex briefly and spin down.
Run the RT reaction following the program.
Prepare PCR mix for cDNA amplification.
Add 15 μL of PCR mix to each well.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal, vortex briefly and spin down.
Run PCR to amplify the cDNA.
Before starting the purification of cDNA, equilibrate Ampure XP beads at room temperature for 15 min.
Vortex thoroughly to ensure that the beads are properly suspended in the buffer.
Add 16.25 μL of Ampure XP beads (0.65× ratio) to each well of the 96-well plate.
Cover the plate with an adhesive seal, vortex briefly and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Place the 96-well plate on the magnetic stand for 5 min.
Wash the beads with 200 μL of 80% (vol/vol) ethanol solution twice.
After removing the washing solution, leave the plate at room temperature for approximately 5 min until the beads have dried completely.
Add 22 μL of EB solution to each well.
Mix 10 times with the pipette to resuspend the beads.
Incubate the plate off the magnet for 2 min at room temperature.
Place the plate back on the magnet for 2 min or longer.
Transfer 20 μL of supernatant containing clean cDNA into a new 96-well plate.
Evaluate the quality of the cDNA using an Agilent Fragment Analyzer Instrument with HS NGS Fragment Kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure the concentration of cDNA generated from each sample using PicoGreen.
Normalize cDNA to a concentration of 0.1–0.15 ng/μL in nuclease-free water.
Prepare DNA libraries using Nextera XT DNA Library Preparation Kit (Illumina).
Use 0.75 μL of normalized cDNA in a miniaturized 15% volume (3 μL total) Nextera tagmentation reaction.
Set up miniaturized reactions in a 384-well plate.
